title: The initiative

D0.outcome: Defines the initiative concretely as the ability to make threats the opponent must answer, and says what it costs to keep and to give up.

D1.outcome: Given a position, says who has the initiative by listing the threats and the forced replies.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, chooses between keeping the initiative, cashing it in, and consolidating.

D3.outcome: Predicts how the loss of one tempo reverses roles and tests the claim that White has the initiative by right.

misconceptions: Initiative means making a threat on every move.
White has the initiative by right.
conditions: Give up the initiative only for a material gain under conditions where you can survive his attack and take it back.
A time lead is fragile: keep harassing, support advanced pieces, prevent his key developing move.
contrasts: Equating the initiative with a threat on every move.
'White is morally entitled to attack' (Black equalises routinely).

soft_prereq_notes.TAC.COMBO.D1: the initiative is cashed in through forcing play
